title: APS 02–03 – Arrays and lists
description: Midterm 1 theory: arrays, sparse matrices, singly, doubly and circular linked lists and their complexities.

questions.question: For a given array a[left…right], in which algorithm does the following instruction appear (in pseudocode): copy a[x+1…right] into a[x…right−1]
Complete the sentence so it's true: Inserting an element is harder …

options.text: …at the start of a singly linked list than at the start of an array (A[0])
…at the end of an array (A[n], n is known) than at the end of a singly linked list
…at the start of an array (A[0]) than at the start of a singly linked list

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics is NOT a disadvantage of using arrays?

options.text: Memory may go unused if there are fewer elements than the allocated size
Adding an element at a given position
Access to elements at a specified position

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of the Array data structure?

options.text: it has constant access time to an element via its index
it doesn't store extra helper data in memory (e.g. pointers)
traversing the whole array is fast

questions.question: A dynamically linked list is a set of…

options.text: elements (nodes) containing a value and a pointer to the next node
ordered elements (nodes) containing a value and a pointer to the next node
ordered elements (nodes) containing a value and pointers to an arbitrary number of nodes
ordered elements (nodes) containing a value and a pointer to the next value

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about a singly linked list?

options.text: Adding and deleting elements is simpler than with an array
a singly linked list doesn't allow efficient access to an arbitrary element
a singly linked list can't fill up (unless memory fills up)
a singly linked list needs no extra memory to store a pointer

questions.question: A sparse matrix is:

options.text: a matrix with many zeros that should be compressed
a matrix with zeros that should be compressed in terms of the indexes it uses
a matrix with many zero values that should be compressed in terms of the indexes it uses
a matrix with many zero values that should be compressed memory-wise

questions.question: Which of the following operations is not O(1) for a sorted array? You may assume the elements in the array are distinct.
What is an array?

options.text: A set of nodes, each with a value and a pointer to the next node
A set of elements that can only be accessed from the top
A set of (key, value) pairs stored in arbitrary memory locations
A consecutive set of memory locations, i.e. a set of ordered pairs (index, value), where every index has a corresponding value

questions.question: The advantage of a singly linked list over a one-dimensional array is:

options.text: It uses less memory per element
The number of elements doesn't have to be known in advance
Its elements are stored in one continuous block of memory

questions.question: What is NOT true about the differences between an array and a linked list?

options.text: In linked lists, inserting a new element is only allowed at the start or the end of the list
An array's size is fixed when it is created
Linked lists need extra memory for pointers
Arrays allow access by index in O(1), linked lists don't
